text: Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He removed the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles.
He commanded Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to keep the law and the commandment.
He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom was at peace under him.
He built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was at peace. No one made war against him in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.

He said to Judah, "Let us build up these cities and surround them with walls and towers, with gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God. We sought him, and he has given us rest on every side." So they built, and they prospered.

Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin, carrying small shields and drawing bows. All of them were mighty warriors.

versions.text: Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin, carrying shields and drawing bows. All of them were mighty warriors.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew distinguishes two kinds of shield: the large body shield (tsinnah) of Judah and the smaller round shield (magen) of Benjamin. Rendering the second simply as "shields" loses the contrast that the first clause has already highlighted with "large shields."

text: Then Zerah the Cushite marched out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he advanced as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up their battle lines in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.

Asa called out to the LORD his God: "LORD, there is no one besides you to help the powerless against the mighty. Help us, LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this vast horde. LORD, you are our God; do not let mere mortals prevail against you."

versions.text: Asa called out to the LORD his God: "LORD, there is no one like you to help the powerless against the mighty. Help us, LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this vast horde. LORD, you are our God; do not let mere mortals prevail against you."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew 'ein immekha means "there is none besides you" (no one but you can help), which is a claim of exclusivity rather than comparison; "no one like you" slightly shifts the sense.

text: So the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

Asa and the troops with him pursued them as far as Gerar. The Cushites fell until not one of them was left alive, for they were shattered before the LORD and before his army. And they carried off a very great amount of plunder.

versions.text: Asa and the troops with him pursued them as far as Gerar. The Cushites fell until not one of them was left alive, for they were shattered before the LORD and his army. And the men of Judah carried off a great amount of plunder.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew simply says "they carried off"; specifying "the men of Judah" adds content not in the text. The intensifier me'od ("very") is also unrendered, and repeating "before" matches the Hebrew's twofold lifne.

text: They struck down all the cities around Gerar, for the terror of the LORD had fallen on them. They plundered all those cities, for there was much plunder in them.

versions.text: They also struck down all the settlements around Gerar, for the terror of the LORD had fallen on them. They plundered every town, since there was much to be taken.
versions.explanation: The same Hebrew word (he'arim) is used twice, but the translation renders it first "settlements" and then "town," obscuring the deliberate repetition. Also, "since there was much to be taken" softens the concrete statement that there was abundant plunder in them.

text: They attacked the camps of the herdsmen as well and carried off great numbers of sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
